column2: There's a toy doll with strings running through its limbs and torso; when you loosen them, it crumples in a heap.
Those limbs were piled up exactly like that.
“Good grief...
This is...
this is a body.{r}{p}A human body!”
Mr. Kobayashi shouted, no longer even caring about the snow blowing over him.
{n2} and I stood frozen without a word, staring at that pile of remains where snow had begun to settle.
......Ten minutes later.
All the guests and staff of the inn “Spur” had gathered in the first-floor lounge.
To be precise, everyone except the guest who had become that body...
Only {n2}, Mr. Kobayashi, and I had seen it.
The rest had been driven out of the room by Mr. Kobayashi.
The three of us, with no composure left to explain what we'd seen, could barely manage to sip hot tea in fear.
“Hey,
don't you think it's about time you told us what happened?”
Midori said irritably.
I glanced at Mr. Kobayashi, but he didn't seem to hear Midori's words at all.
I answered, gasping.
“He's dead.{r}{p}Cut to pieces in there...
he's dead.”
I heard someone gulp.
“Cut to pieces...
what do you mean?”
Midori snapped back, perhaps thinking it was a bad joke.
“What do I mean...”
Without realizing it, my voice had gone shrill, almost a scream.
“...He's in pieces!{r}{p}His head,
his hands,
his legs,
they're all severed and lying there!”
“Noooo!”
One of the girls cried out and burst into tears.
It was Aki.
“...Is it that
Mr. Tanaka guy?”
Midori asked in a low voice.
“Yes...
I think so.{r}{p}The color of his face was completely different, so I can't be sure, but I think it was him.”
Suddenly Midori narrowed her eyes.
“Couldn't it be a really well-made dummy?{r}{p}Same as that threatening note, a prank?”
“I wouldn't mistake a dummy for a person.”
I remembered the cut surface at what looked like a shoulder joint, and shuddered.
“But, you know,
movie special effects are amazing these days, right?{r}{p}Maybe that sort of thing.”
Hearing that, my confidence began to wane.
That was a human being.{r}{p}No mistake.
There was blood too.”
When Mr. Kobayashi declared this, Aki cried out again.{g}
“I knew it, the threatening note was real!
I want to go home!”
“Come to think of it...
I've heard about this.
...About the kamaitachi.”
Mr. Mikimoto began to speak, licking his lips.
“Kamaitachi?”
I asked back.
“Yeah.

You know it, right?{r}{p}In this area, since long ago, it's been known that clothes suddenly slice open or people get hurt where there's nothing around.{r}{p}The locals thought it was the work of a weasel-like creature carrying a sickle
and called it kamaitachi.”
Mr. Mikimoto spoke in a low voice and looked around at our faces.
After a pause, Mr. Kobayashi snorted.
“You're saying the kamaitachi tore Mr. Tanaka apart?{r}{p}Ridiculous.”
{n2} cut in too.
“Besides, isn't kamaitachi a natural phenomenon?{r}{p}I've heard it's something about a vacuum forming and cutting things.”
But Mr. Mikimoto didn't flinch.
“That explanation does exist.{r}{p}But whether it's a monster or a natural phenomenon, something like that definitely happens.”
“But I've heard of cuts and torn clothes, not of a person being cut into pieces.”
I said.
“If it's the work of a monster, anything is conceivable.{r}{p}...Don't make that face.{r}{p}I don't really believe in monsters, you know.{r}{p}Let's say it's a natural phenomenon
{r}{p}Listen to this wind.{r}{p}With wind this fierce, it wouldn't be strange if a terrifying vacuum, rarer than rare, formed.{r}{p}Don't you think so?”
A wind that shatters a window and instantly cuts apart a person standing at it...
Had a wind like that really blown?
“It's plasma!
It's the work of plasma.”
Aki, who had been wearing a frightened look all along, cried out.
“Aki...
what's plasma?”
Keiko asked doubtfully.
“I don't really know, but
it's got to be.{r}{p}That would explain it.”
It didn't seem to explain anything, but Aki nodded with complete conviction.
“Then what about the threatening note?{r}{p}A human wrote that, didn't they?”
“Well, but...
but...”
At Kanako's words, Aki, still looking troubled, started crying again.
“Hey, I been listenin' this whole time, but this threatening note,
what the heck's that about?”
Mr. Kayama cut in, unable to hold back.
Mr. Kobayashi glanced at me for a moment.
But he soon seemed to realize there was no point hiding it now, and began to tell about the threatening note bit by bit.
“Actually...”
When he finished, everyone was speechless for a while.
“Something like that
happened?”
Mr. Mikimoto murmured.
“Ya gotta tell us things like that up front, y'know. What a pain...”
Mr. Kayama grumbled with a sigh.
“...But what's done is done.{r}{p}Anyway, if that thing upstairs really is a body, we gotta call the police quick.”
The police!
I hadn't realized something that obvious until now.
Having been shown something so abnormal, I seemed to have lost the ability to think straight.
Mr. Kobayashi was apparently the same; he turned around in a hurry and went to the phone.
He picked up the receiver and put it to his ear.
But soon he started jabbing the hook irritably.
“No good.
There's no sound.{r}{p}The phone's dead!”
“Wh-
what d'ya mean!”
Mr. Kayama stood up and shouted.
“That's a problem!”
“Probably the line got cut somewhere.”
Mr. Kobayashi glared hatefully at the silent receiver.
The phone is dead...!
It took a while for the meaning of that to sink into my head.
If we couldn't use the phone, then unless the blizzard stopped by tomorrow, we couldn't contact the police.
...And not only that, we couldn't get down from here either.
Mr. Kayama suddenly burst out laughing.
“Oh yeah!
I got a cell phone.{r}{p}I'll just use that.”
But Mr. Kobayashi said flatly:
“It's no use, Mr. Kayama.{r}{p}There's no signal around here.{r}{p}Cell phones don't work.”
“Th-
then what the heck do we do?
With a murderer wanderin' around here.”
A murderer...
The word caught us off guard.
Distracted by the strangeness of the body, we hadn't considered that it was plainly murder, and had been fussing about kamaitachi and plasma.
Or maybe we had deliberately avoided thinking it.
But there was no way that was an accident or suicide.
Murder was the most natural conclusion.
Someone had killed Mr. Tanaka and cut up his body.
And as Mr. Kayama said, given this weather, the culprit was quite likely still around.
“Do you think we could get down the mountain in this weather?”
When I asked, Mr. Kobayashi and Toshio shook their heads at almost the same time.
“Impossible.”
It was Toshio who answered.

“Even Mr. Mikimoto's making it here earlier was a miracle.{r}{p}On foot you'd freeze to death on the way; by car, even if you're lucky, you'd get stranded.{r}{p}If you're unlucky, you could plunge into a ravine.”
“Then wouldn't the killer try to hide inside this inn?{r}{p}That's the only way to survive, isn't it?”
Everyone held their breath.
Even Aki, who had been crying, stopped for a moment and showed a look of terror.
Toshio stood up angrily.
“Then...
then what? We spend the night with a guy who chopped up a body?{r}{p}You've got to be kidding!”
“That's right.
No way anyone can sleep easy with a murderer maybe around.{r}{p}We gotta do somethin'.”
Mr. Kayama nodded vigorously too.
“Do something...
like what?”
Mr. Kobayashi asked back, bewildered.
“Well, catch him, what else?{r}{p}Since the police can't come, we gotta catch him ourselves, don't we?”
wait a minute.”
The one who made a pitiful voice, in contrast to his looks, was Mr. Mikimoto.

“We're talking about a vicious killer who murdered a man and cut up his body, aren't we?{r}{p}Rather than recklessly going after him, isn't it better for everyone to stay put here?{r}{p}With this many people,
even the most vicious criminal wouldn't be able to make a move...”
“So you're sayin' we all stay up forever here?{r}{p}We might all get slaughtered while we sleep.”
Because Mr. Kayama came out with such a terrible thing, the girls looked more frightened than ever.
I hurriedly cut in.
“No,
no matter how awful the guy is, he wouldn't go that far.{r}{p}Though I do think we need to lock everything up tight.”
“Lockin' up don't help if he's already inside.”
“Impossible!
When and from where would he have gotten in?”
Mr. Kobayashi shouted in surprise.
“How should I know.{r}{p}But somebody's been killed, ain't that a fact?{r}{p}He musta come in without us noticin', right?”
“But...
but...”
Mr. Kobayashi searched for words.
“Hey,
the window was broken, wasn't it?{r}{p}Maybe he came in through the window?{r}{p}They don't clear snow much out back, so climbin' in a second-floor window ain't that hard, I bet.”
“Even so, wouldn't the killer have left through the window again?{r}{p}The door was still locked, after all...”
I said what I thought was only natural.
“How should I know?

The doors here have push-button locks.{r}{p}Even if he came in by the window, he could've just pushed the door button to lock it after. He could've hidden in a vacant room upstairs, or slipped downstairs while we were up there.”
On the door point, Mr. Kayama was right.
Push the button from the inside and it locks...
Every guest room door at “Spur” was that type.
So just because the door was locked didn't mean the killer had escaped through the window.
Even so, we had just checked all the second-floor rooms together.
It was hard to imagine someone slipping downstairs under the eyes of us milling around the hallway.
“Whatever the case, shouldn't we all get something to use as a weapon?”
{n2}, who had been silent and pale, spoke up.
I was surprised by her suggestion, but...
“Yeah, good idea.
Just in case.”
“Let's get ready right away.”
Everyone agreed at once.
...But in an inn like this, there were hardly any weapons.
In the end, what everyone picked up was{p}ski poles,
a fruit knife,
and a mop handle.
Kitchen knives were judged too dangerous, so it came down to these...
Not exactly reassuring.
“We'll form teams and search every inch.{r}{p}Under the beds,
in the closets,
the bathtubs...{p}we don't know where he's hidin'.”
Mr. Kayama had somehow taken the lead.
Maybe that's just what company presidents do.
Five men.
Me,
Mr. Mikimoto,
Mr. Kobayashi,
Mr. Kayama,
and Toshio...
That was all.
The women were all staying behind.
I wished someone would sew me a good-luck charm belt.
“Be careful.”
{n2}'s single remark was my only emotional support.
“Where's the best place to start?”
Mr. Kobayashi asked no one in particular.
I said.
“Let's search the second floor first.”
“You two go first.”
Even though it was his idea, Mr. Kayama sent Mr. Mikimoto and me ahead.
It couldn't be helped.
I gripped a ski pole, Mr. Mikimoto gripped the mop handle, and we climbed the stairs to the second floor.
I just hoped it wouldn't be a stairway to heaven.
When Mr. Kobayashi unlocked the door, Mr. Mikimoto and I readied our “weapons.”
“Okay, opening it.”
As soon as we nodded, Mr. Kobayashi opened the door and hid behind it.
Then we went in, thrusting out our ski pole and mop
ahead of us.
We searched each room that way, even under the beds.
Since it would be risky for everyone to go into one room and let him escape in the meantime, only Mr. Mikimoto and I went in.
At first we were jumpy, but as we repeated the same thing, we grew bolder.
Mr. Mikimoto seemed to be the same; his face had returned to normal color.
“No matter who shows up, f-five of us should be fine, right...”
“S-sure.
There are five of us, after all...”
We finally finished checking all the guest rooms, but found no sign of anyone.
“Kobayashi, what's that door?”
Mr. Kayama pointed at the door at the end of the hall.
“That's a storeroom for cleaning supplies and such.{r}{p}A person
could hide in there, I suppose, but...”
Everyone froze with a start.
Mr. Mikimoto looked at me, eyes bulging.
'Did you hear that?'
His eyes said as much.
I gulped and nodded firmly.
Sweat seeped onto the hand gripping my ski pole.
Mr. Kobayashi, hand on the knob, looked around at everyone.
Me, Mr. Mikimoto, Toshio, and, from a bit farther back, Mr. Kayama...
The four of us nodded in unison.
The door opened.
Inside were buckets of cleaning supplies, brooms, dustpans, and rubber slippers and other washroom items.
With no light, we could see only the shadows of those things.
is anyone there?”
Mr. Mikimoto called into the darkness.
I let out a breath of relief.
“See? The killer must have escaped through the window.{r}{p}He wouldn't try to hide in a place with this many people...”
Just as I said that,
there was a sudden clatter and a broom came toppling toward us.
waaah!
S-stay back!”
Mr. Mikimoto shut his eyes and swung the mop handle around.
“...A cat.”
“That's Jenny.
So that's where she was.”
Toshio said.
“Jenny?”
“The cat we keep here.{r}{p}I hadn't seen her and wondered where she'd gone.{r}{p}Never thought she'd crawled in here.”
“Come on.”
Mr. Kobayashi urged everyone on.
“Next is the first floor.”
Everyone seemed to be starting to think there was almost no chance the killer had gotten in.
Unlike before, they went down to the first floor completely relaxed.
“I may not look it, but I did judo in high school.{r}{p}If the culprit shows up, I'll flip him with a one-arm shoulder throw, pin him down, and he won't dare peep.”
Mr. Kayama started saying that now of all times.
“Then why don't you take the lead this time, Mr. Kayama?”
When I said it sarcastically, Mr. Kayama flustered.
“...I'd love to, but
my back's actin' up right now.{r}{p}Ow, ow, ow.
Dang it, if only my back were better...”
I was no match for this old guy.
On the first floor, {n2} and the others were waiting with worried faces.
“How was it?”
To {n2}'s question I only shook my head.
The black cat that had scared us was now wolfing down food at Midori's feet.
Totally oblivious to our feelings...
On the first floor, apart from the lounge,
there were the dining room and kitchen.
The staff rooms of Midori, Toshio, and the others.
The Kobayashis' room.
The drying room, and so on.
We looked through them all quickly, but it was hard to imagine anyone hiding there...
“Aren't there any other rooms?”
I asked Mr. Kobayashi as we returned to the lounge.
“Only the wine cellar, but that's locked.”
Mr. Kobayashi answered after thinking a moment.
“Well,
so there was nobody after all.{r}{p}Too bad.
And I was all set to treat him to my Death Wheel throw.”
Mr. Kayama rubbed his hands in frustration.
Still all talk, that guy.
Back in the lounge, Kyoko had made coffee for us.
“Nobody was there?”
{n2} said, reading our faces.
“So the killer must have escaped outside after all.”
“Probably.”
Toshio answered.
Everyone wore complex expressions, relieved yet uneasy.
Naturally.
Although nothing dangerous had happened for now, we still couldn't be sure that no one was really hiding.
And even if no one was here now, he might come in during the night.
No matter how well we locked up, he could get in easily by smashing a window.
...Wait a minute.
A question suddenly occurred to me.
From the start, we had all assumed the killer broke a window to get in.
But was that really so?
I noticed that one among us had no alibi.
When the sound of the window breaking came, there was exactly one person who hadn't been in the lounge.
The man sitting next to me, enjoying his hot coffee...
Toshio.
This man could have killed Mr. Tanaka.
I peeked at his face.
A cheerful college student who loved skiing.
Could that have been just an act?
“Hm?
What's up?”
Toshio looked back at me.
“Oh, um...”
the sugar?
My bad.”
Toshio passed me the sugar pot.
“Th-thanks.”
With no choice, I took it and put sugar in my coffee.
Apparently he'd misread what my stare meant.
Could this seemingly good-natured guy be the killer...?
No...
Whatever the circumstances, there was no way this man could kill someone and chop up the body.
The killer had escaped outside after all.
He had to be a hardened criminal with no connection to anyone here.
Yes,
Mr. Tanaka, who was killed, was probably a yakuza or something too.
And he was killed by a different yakuza.
I tried to force myself to believe that.
Suddenly Mr. Kobayashi shot to his feet.
“What's wrong?”
I asked.
“...I'm going to check outside.”
“Outside?
Why?”
“...There might be some trace.{r}{p}Footprints, tire tracks, that sort of thing.”
Toshio shook his head.
“Even if there were, they'd be long gone in this snow.”
“True, but...{r}{p}the murderer might come back here, and we can't just do nothing.”
Mr. Kobayashi said bitterly.
“I'll go with you.”
I stood up.
“You'll come too, right, Mr. Kayama?{r}{p}If we run into the killer outside, you'll use your Death Wheel on him, won't you?”
When I said that sarcastically, Mr. Kayama answered, stammering.
w-
well, yeah.{r}{p}...But it's cold outside, ain't it?{r}{p}I, uh,
ain't good with the cold.{r}{p}If ya find him, drive him inside.{r}{p}I'll treat him to my Swallow Reversal.”
He's just like Ikkyu {C3}(a clever monk from folktales){C0}.
Besides, I don't think the Swallow Reversal is a judo move...
In the end, four of us, Mr. Kobayashi, Toshio, Mr. Mikimoto, and I, would make the rounds outside.
We all went back to our rooms to change and met at the entrance five minutes later, at ten o'clock sharp.
Once the four of us were together, we put on our boots, took our “weapons,” and headed out.
The moment we opened the door, a razor-edged wind attacked along with the snow.
I hurriedly pulled up my hood and cinched the cord tight.
“We'll go around, one from the right and one from the left.”
Mr. Kobayashi raised his voice to beat the wind.
“{n1} and I will go clockwise, Toshio and Mr. Mikimoto counterclockwise.{r}{p}Sound good?”
Everyone nodded.
Stepping off the porch, we found a white hell.
Split into two groups, we started walking, sinking shin-deep in the ever-deepening snow.
“Don't get separated!”
Mr. Kobayashi shouted at the backs of Toshio and the others vanishing into the blizzard.
But the howling wind drowned out his voice at once.
Even with my hood cinched tight and my head down, the wind slashed my face without mercy.
“I can't...
I can't see anything like this!”
Even when I raised my head and forced my eyes open, the raging white darkness hid everything past a meter.
My fingers gripping the ski pole were already freezing, even through gloves.
“Mr. Kobayashi!
Mr. Kobayashi!”
Having lost sight of him, I shouted in near panic.
Wherever I looked, snow, snow, snow.
I couldn't even see the shadow of the inn.
I had lost all sense of direction.
Anyway, I tried heading right.
But no matter how far I went, there was nothing to go by.
Just swirling snow.
“Mr. Kobayashi!
Where are you?”
My voice cracked with fear.
My bare cheeks froze and went numb.
I thought I'd better go back.
I tried going back the way I thought I'd come.
But...
though I must have gone a long way, there was no sign of the inn.
I decided to keep pushing on.
Suddenly something like a blow hit my head, and I fell backward into the snow.
It felt like sinking into a soft feather quilt...
A strange sensation, both cold and warm.
If I hadn't heard someone's shout then, I might have fallen asleep right there.
{n1}!{r}{p}Over here!
Hurry!”
Mr. Kobayashi's shout threaded through gaps in the piercing wind and reached my ears.
I struggled, rolled, and finally got up out of the snow.
A throbbing pain shot through the top of my head.
Looking up, I saw the wall of “Spur” right there.
The “blow” I'd felt was apparently just me crashing into it.
Amazed at my own stupidity, I was flooded with relief.
Where are you! {n1}!”
I heard the voice call me again.
“I'm here!”
Shouting back, I started walking along the wall.
In the shelter of the building, the wind was not as fierce as before.
Walking through deep snow was hard labor in itself.
My hands and feet were numb with cold, yet sweat had begun on my back and I was out of breath.
Finally I reached the back corner of the building, rounded it, and saw Mr. Kobayashi's back.
“Mr. Kobayashi!”
I called as I approached.
At Mr. Kobayashi's feet lay Mr. Mikimoto.
Toshio was trying to lift him up.
what happened?”
Mr. Mikimoto groaned from the ground.
A red streak ran down from his temple.
Blood.
“This is...”
“Looks like somebody hit him.”
We have to get him inside and treat him.”
Toshio said.
“Hit him?”
Who?”
As I asked, I realized it was a stupid question.
Of course, it had to be whoever killed Mr. Tanaka.
“If I hadn't fallen behind, I could've caught him...”
Toshio said bitterly.
“Why did you separate?”
Mr. Kobayashi demanded, though not in a blaming tone.
He himself had also lost track of me.
With this visibility, it couldn't be helped.
I shielded myself from the wind with my hand and strained my eyes.
The snow around where Mr. Mikimoto lay was churned up as if there had been a struggle.
But I couldn't tell whether there were footprints.
What's more, the falling snow was quickly covering even our own tracks.
“Damn it.
If only we had a dog...”
Toshio bit his lip and glared into the white darkness.
But would any sane person try to flee into this blizzard?
The instant I thought that, I shuddered.
Wasn't there no one out here but us?
Could Toshio have been the one who hit Mr. Mikimoto?
Lying about falling behind, and hitting Mr. Mikimoto from behind with a mop handle...
“Anyway, let's carry him.”
Mr. Kobayashi gathered the “weapons,” I took Mr. Mikimoto's legs, and Toshio supported his shoulders.
He was heavier than expected.
Could we really carry a person back along a path that was hard enough just to walk?
Uneasy, I started back the way we had come.
“Not that way!”
Mr. Kobayashi yelled.
Apparently there was a back door.
I felt a little relieved.
Even so, carrying a limp, unconscious big man through deep snow made even a few steps hard.
Before we'd gone even ten meters, my shoulders felt ready to pop out of their sockets.
Toshio gritted his teeth and endured too.
Before long we stopped.
Mr. Kobayashi rang a bell.
I couldn't see anything, but we seemed to have reached the back door.
Hurry...
someone hurry up and open it...
After an agonizing wait, the door finally opened.
We tumbled inside, looking like snowmen.
Inside, Kyoko stood frozen with a hand over her mouth.
“...Quick
...quick, treat him.”
Gasping for breath, Mr. Kobayashi could manage only that much.
Kyoko was shocked and couldn't move for a while.
But when she noticed Mr. Mikimoto was bleeding, she called toward the back.
“Midori.
Quick, come here!”
Before long, Midori arrived, and she and the Kobayashis, three in all, dragged Mr. Mikimoto toward the back.
Toshio closed the back door.
I lay on the floor, without the energy to stand.
“...Still,
why would he get attacked?”
Once he'd caught his breath a little, Toshio said.
I wonder... Maybe he ran into the killer.”
I swallowed the words, Wasn't it you who did it?

“But where he was is right outside the room with the body, isn't it?{r}{p}Even if whoever killed that Tanaka guy escaped by the window, would he have stayed there all that time?{r}{p}He'd have turned into an ice sculpture.”
That was certainly true.
But I no longer felt like taking Toshio's words at face value.
“Maybe he came back there for some reason.{r}{p}You know how they say,
the criminal always returns to the scene of the crime.”
I gave a random answer off the top of my head.
But surprisingly, Toshio reacted strongly to my words.
“That's it!
That's it!{r}{p}The killer went back there.
For some reason.{r}{p}
...Maybe he realized he'd left some evidence behind and went back.”
What was this man thinking, saying this?
Wasn't he the one who hit him?
Was the killer still outside after all?
Or someone else besides Toshio...
Mr. Kobayashi?
Mr. Kobayashi had had the chance to attack Mr. Mikimoto too.
Leave me behind, walk ahead fast, and hit Mr. Mikimoto when he ran into him...
But even if he could have hit Mr. Mikimoto,
he couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka.
When it happened, Mr. Kobayashi had been in the lounge with us.
If the killer wasn't Toshio, the only possibility was that he'd escaped outside, but...
Either way, it was all still speculation.
Once Mr. Mikimoto regained consciousness, it would be clearer.
Who hit him.
What it felt like.
Even if he hadn't seen the culprit's face clearly, we might get some clue.
“Anyway, let's get back to the rooms.”
Toshio stood up.
“How about you, can you stand?”
He held out a hand to me.
“...Thanks.”
After hesitating a little, I carefully took his hand and stood up.
Toshio went back to his room.
I watched his back vanish into the room and then headed for the lounge.
I couldn't bring myself to turn my back on someone who might be a murderer.
Passing through the lounge, I found only Haruko and {n2} there.
“Where is everyone?”
“Mr. Kayama went back to his room after you went out.{r}{p}He said he wanted to try his cell phone again...”
“And Kanako and the others said they wanted to use the bathroom...”
“All three together?”
“Yes...
And Midori took Mr. Mikimoto to his room with Uncle and the others.”
“Yeah, I know about that.”
I realized my clothes were soaked through with melted snow.
“I'm going to go change.”
Saying that, I went up to the second floor.
“Oh,
Mr. Kayama.”
I ran into Mr. Kayama just as I stepped into the hallway after changing.
“Oh, it's you...
Thanks for yer trouble.”
“How was the phone?”
“Phone?
Oh, the cell phone.{r}{p}No good, no good.
Still no good.{r}{p}Kobayashi was right.”
“I see...”
Only {n2} and Haruko were in the lounge, as before.
The others were probably still in Mr. Mikimoto's room.
“Oof.”
Mr. Kayama sat on the sofa.
Figuring the sofa would get crowded again, I sat on the stairs.
how'd it go?{r}{p}What's it like outside?{r}{p}Find anything strange?”
Mr. Kayama had been in his room all this time and apparently still knew nothing.
“This isn't the time for that.{r}{p}Mr. Mikimoto was attacked by someone!”
“What d'ya mean?”
Mr. Kayama knit his brows.
“Who's 'someone'?
Did he get away already?”
“W-well...
nobody saw it,
nobody but Mr. Mikimoto.”
{n2} and Haruko listened anxiously too.
“So is he hurt bad?{r}{p}Or is he already...”
He seemed to swallow the word dead.
“I don't know.
Mr. Kobayashi and Midori should be treating him now, but...”
“Don't tell me he's plannin' to kill us off one by one.”
This old guy came out with something outrageous again.
{n2} and Haruko both gave a start for a moment.
“...That could be.”
I trembled with fear.
Mr. Kayama too...”
{n2} cried out.
“Please don't say reckless things.{r}{p}He's not a serial killer, why would he do such terrible things...
But Mr. Kayama held to his theory.
“But if he kills us all, he can wait out the blizzard here in peace.{r}{p}Besides, with nobody left to report to the police, he can take his time thinkin' about how to escape.”
“That's...
that's too awful!”
